name: World WAR! Championship
epitaph: The fed's own top prize, crowned in a 16-man tournament won by Brutus Noir at the promotion's own second-ever show and changing hands at least nine times since — through Inner City Firmer, Seth Blitzspear, Noir again, Randy Blake, J.R. Death, Stein "Ice" Berg, and Tonnage — before Jason Midnight was crowned via a separate UWC interfed tournament and carried it into the fed's own Dec 1996 supercard.

name: International WAR! Championship
epitaph: WAR!'s original secondary belt, crowned in an inaugural tournament won by Bludgeon days after the promotion's own launch and passed through Johnny Thunder and Butch Williams before Jerry "Goon" Gordon's October 1995 win made him, per the show's own text, the first wrestler to hold two WAR! titles at once; Booster Dunne, Williams again, and "Magnum" Biff McGriff followed across 1996, McGriff winning it off a slow three-count the show's own text calls "tainted... but a victory nonetheless."

name: World WAR! Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A tag title that changed hands at least five times across this pull's own read shows, from the Brotherhood through the Star Smashers, the Aderondac Brothers and Industrial Revolution to the Annihilators, the last won with a moonsault off the roof of a parked van in the WARena parking lot.

name: WAR! Liberty Championship
epitaph: A title born at the Season 2 relaunch opener, when The Mandarin won it from a debuting Joey the Clown (the future DeathJester), then lost it within the week to Jerry "Goon" Gordon's same-week double-title run; a hot-potato stretch followed — Joey the Clown regaining it under his own future ring name, then Sid Starr, then "008" Jim Bondo twice in one night after a retiring Butch Williams signed it over by contract clause — before it settled, by late 1996, on DeathJester and then "Dirty" Doug Simpkins.

name: WAR!Lord Championship
epitaph: A title contested through a running succession involving Big Duke, CrocMaster, American Patriot and Robski, the last "regaining" it in a cage match at the fed's own Dec 1996 supercard after an earlier, off-page reign of his own.

name: International WAR! Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Created in an interfed tag tournament won by DangerZone at CivilWar 1 in June 1995, this title's own record then gaps until Kalifornia Heat, already champions, retained it against the All-Americans in a Texas Death match at the fed's own Dec 1996 supercard.

name: Freedom Championship
epitaph: A Season 1 singles belt created by fiat when the fed's own first tag title was declared defunct, changing hands four times across a single month (Trailboss Mike Dallas, the Maltese Falcon twice, and Bombsquad) before this pull's own read window ends with Falcon still champion.

name: WAR! Tag Team Championship (Season 1, defunct)
epitaph: The fed's own first-ever championship, won on its debut card and declared defunct by in-story fiat eleven days later, replaced by the singles Freedom Championship; never contested again.

name: National WAR! Championship
epitaph: Born from a 14-man battle royale during the fed's own August 1997 relaunch under new ownership in Manhattan, contested twice in three weeks and still active when the fed's own 'Old War!'/'New War!' rosters reunified that October.

name: WAR! Manhattan Championship
epitaph: A borough-named singles title contested through WAR!'s 1999 season, changing hands once in a masked-opponent swerve.
